output.brief: The problem is the Arnholt resin combined with the degraded D5 dryer, not the people or the resin alone. Arnholt lots run through D5 reject at about 10%, while the same resin through the healthy D7 or a portable dryer (PD-1) rejects at about 0.8%. Quillan resin through D5 is normal at 0.9%, so D5 alone is not enough. The six new operators reject at the same rate as experienced staff on the same material (9.9% vs 10.3% on Arnholt), so the performance plans in A1 would be unfair and would not fix anything. This week: repair D5's heater and desiccant, confirm dew point is back near -40 °C, restore the original alarm limit, keep Arnholt off D5 until verified, and add a moisture check on each VX resin lot. Keep the Arnholt annex storage question open; it is untested. Confidence is good on the D5 finding. The one caveat is that Arnholt samples all came from the unconditioned annex, so storage may also contribute, which I did not confirm.
